messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 - Customer private traffic degradation (AcmeCorp) -> eu-west-3a transit path. Elevated 5xx and packet loss on Direct Attach. Auto-paged oncall.
sara: taking pager, on it. tagging net.
mike: looking — I see repeated BGP withdraws from our primary DX peer (203.0.113.5). multiple short-lived prefixes flapping.
eli: customer slacked ops that application retries are spiking. confirmed errors correlate with the BGP flap windows.
brynn: I'm on call w/ customer now — they see ~30-60% packet loss for their private subnet (10.10.0.0/16). asking for immediate failover to backup if possible.
mike: quick snapshot from edge:```
Neighbor 203.0.113.5 AS 65001 - State: ESTABLISHED
Routes for 10.10.0.0/16: best via 203.0.113.5 (localpref 100)
Observed withdraws: 12 in last 10m, AS PATH changed between 65001 and 65500
Interface counters: drops on DX primary phys0 ~ 3.2k pkts/min
```
sara: thanks. if primary is flapping but secondary (203.0.113.9) is stable, we can prefer secondary via localpref override. is that safe?
mike: yes. we'll push a temporary policy to increase localpref for 203.0.113.9 to 200 for the Acme prefixes. that should steer traffic immediately and avoid app-level retries.
sara: preparing policy now. applying to transit-gw route table for eu-west-3a. small blast radius, will monitor.
ops-bot: Deploying route-policy "acme-temp-failover" to tg-eu-west-3a...
ops-bot: Deployment succeeded (job id: dp-8743).
jun: I can see route-table change — routes for 10.10.0.0/16 now prefer 203.0.113.9 (localpref 200). BGP convergence in progress.
eli: starting tcpdump on customer-facing interface to capture errors. attaching snippet to ticket.
brynn: just told customer: "We've moved your private traffic to your backup Direct Attach while we work with the provider on primary path instability. We'll monitor for 60-90m and update." they appreciated the quick switch.
incidentbot: Metric update: 5xx rate for Acme private traffic down from 18% -> 2.1% in last 5m. Latency normalized.
mike: provider ticket opened (TELCO-4521). shared BGP logs + pcap. asking for root cause (likely SP internal maintenance or flapping aggregation).
pagerduty: Escalation: provider NOC paged at 2024-11-03T23:20Z.
sara: good. I'll keep the policy in place for now; plan: monitor 1h, if stable, we will keep and then coordinate a controlled revert with provider.
jun: adding health check: if primary becomes stable and BGP steady for 20m, we'll perform a gradual localpref rollback (staged 50% -> 100%).
eli: handing off now — i'm heading to other pager. eli takes over monitoring for next 60m.
eli: taking over. will post updates every 15m or on any regression.
brynn: I've sent the customer a summary + incident link. asked them to validate app behavior; they confirmed lower error rates.
incidentbot: Post-mitigation snapshot: BGP state stable (no withdraws in last 12m), packet loss on primary interface trending to zero but provider still investigating.
mike: note for postmortem: capture timestamps of BGP flaps, cpus, interface counters, and provider change windows. attach to TELCO-4521.
sara: agreed. I'll set up a short incident ticket with timeline + who acted. tagging mike/jun/eli/brynn.
ops-bot: oncall handoff reminder — next oncall is mike at 2024-11-04T00:45Z.
eli: confirming monitoring alerts suppressed for the temporary policy to avoid noise.
brynn: customer asked for RCA once provider responds. I've requested that and will coordinate delivery.
incidentbot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> traffic moved to backup DX. provider engaged. Next update expected in 60m.
sara: closing active P1 page for now; keeping incident open as mitigated until provider confirms.
eli: will escalate if any regression. logging final note here and will add to postmortem draft.
